accuracy.evidence: Matches Development Matters (2021) PSED for 3-4 year olds (become more independent in meeting own care needs, e.g. dressing) and the EYFS ELG Managing Self (manage own basic hygiene and personal needs, including dressing). The order rules were checked by hand: trousers need pants; shoes need socks and trousers; the coat needs the other four, so the only refusals are outer-before-inner. Tops 2 and 4 show the label at the front (turn round), tops 1 and 3 show the star (ready). Pairs start swapped, right, swapped and pass only when the half-smileys meet. Buttons accept only the lowest undone button and only its own hole. The coat flip order (coat on the floor inside up, stand by the hood, arms in, flip over the head) is the standard nursery method. Parameterised answers n-1, n, 3+n and n hold at the corners of their ranges.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the dressing slips named in the adult text: outer before inner (dress-scene refusals, socks predict, p1, m1, m7, challenge 'order'), back to front with the label at the front (label predict, top sort feedback, p4, m9, challenge 'label'), shoes on the wrong feet (pair check feedback, p5, challenge 'feet'), buttons in the wrong hole or out of order (button predict and hole feedback, m3, challenge 'button'), and a grown-up doing it all instead of help with the tricky bit (m5, challenge 'help').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdress is built on dressing itself: a drawn child who gains pants, trousers, socks, shoes and a coat only in an inside-first order, children in tops drawn with either a star on the front or the label showing at the neck, a pair of shoes that mirror when tapped with a half-smiley sticker in each, a coat whose buttons slide into the hole beside them from the bottom up, and the four coat-flip steps. The going-out routine in flagroutine (lesson 251) is about remembering a sequence of daily tasks; this lab teaches the body rules (layers, front and back, left and right, button alignment) that a routine cannot.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each rule by trying: shoes dropped on the child before socks are refused with 'Shoes go over socks', the Put them on key only works once the two sticker halves meet, an upper button is refused with 'start at the bottom' and a wrong hole with 'the coat would be wonky', and a flip card in the wrong space names the step that comes first. The done messages state the rule only after the scene has shown it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Shoes' first (the shoes are refused until the socks are on), 'At the front, so I can see it' for the label (those tops sort into Turn it round), 'Any one' for which button to start with (only the bottom one is accepted), and 'By the bottom of the coat' for the coat flip (Stand by the hood is step 2).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions whose wrong options carry five tagged messages: order (next to your skin goes on first: pants before trousers, socks before shoes), label (the label goes at the back; turn it round), feet (swap until the halves make a smiley), button (start at the bottom, use the hole next to it) and help (have a go first, then ask for help with just the tricky bit). Answer order rotates per question.

readability.evidence: For ages 3 to 4 the kid paragraphs use very short sentences and everyday words (pants, socks, label, smiley); each lab prompt gives one action and the canvas labels are one short line. Development Matters and ELG terms stay in the adult text; the validator's kid and adult readability limits pass.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: inside layers first, label at the back, the sticker trick, buttons from the bottom and asking for help with one bit. Adult paragraphs: EYFS placement, how to make success easy plus the coat flip, five named mistakes, what each lab scene does. The content gate's filler and 12% duplicate checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark: the child sits left with five full-width clothing tiles (about 65 px tall) on the right, four tops fit one row above two tall sorting boxes, the shoe pair is about 115 px across with a 220 px Put them on key, the coat buttons are 36 px circles with holes beside them, and the four coat-flip spaces fill the width with two-line cards below. The iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me.

accessibility.evidence: Each canvas action has a labelled button twin: Put on each item of clothing, each top to Ready or Turn round, Swap the shoes and Put them on, Button N then Hole N, and each coat-flip card to a nearby numbered step. The canvas aria-label reports every refusal and success in words; axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs clean in light and dark themes.

sources: DfE (2021) Development Matters: Personal, Social and Emotional Development, 3 and 4 year olds (become more independent in meeting their own care needs, e.g. dressing)
DfE (2024) Statutory framework for the EYFS, ELG Managing Self (manage their own basic hygiene and personal needs, including dressing)
NHS Start for Life / NHS (2023) Helping your child get dressed: lay clothes out in order, start with undressing, choose easy fastenings
Nursery practice: the coat flip method and the half-sticker trick for shoes, as described in EYFS self-care guidance
